messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: SEV2 detected - elevated 5xx rate and latency in eu-west-1 (traffic spike + provider flakiness). Auto-alerting on-call.
olivia: seeing ~15% 5xx at the edge for eu-west-1, errors concentrated on generation endpoints (/v1/generate, /v1/chat). New rel tries show KV cache thrashing.
raj: confirm - metrics dashboard: error_rate(eu-west-1) spiked at 14.8% around 09:12 UTC; p90 latency jumped to 1.2s. Provider X shows increased packet loss from 09:05.
mike: who is oncall? I’m SRE shadow but not primary.
incident-bot: Paging nate (sre-oncall) + jess (infra) + emily (runtime).
emily: onsite, looking at logs now. Traces show lots of backend OOMs on reranker-worker instances.
jess: provider X is dropping connections intermittently at the edge, we have some routed to provider Y but not enough capacity in eu to absorb.
olivia: customer-impact: partial thumbnails for some customers, higher latency on embeddings & generation for EU users. CS reported 2 enterprise customers noticing timeouts.
support-bot: Customer alert: sent a status update to the two affected enterprise tenants at 09:30 UTC.
mike: mitigation suggestions: 1) short-term: reduce per-tenant QPS in EU, 2) disable expensive reranker path for EU, 3) failover some routes to provider Y / us-east-2 region, 4) drain a subset of overloaded instances.
raj: agree. prioritize options that reduce memory pressure quickly: disable reranker-v2 in eu-west-1 and enable simple-rank fallback.
emily: I can flip the feature flag now: `featureset toggle reranker-v2 --region eu-west-1 --off`
olivia: go ahead but coordinate with CS message. If we turn it off, expect slight quality regression for reranking customers. Note customers: acme-inc, datawise.
jess: starting a gradual drain of 20% of overloaded worker pool in eu-west-1 to reduce churn: `rwctl drain --region eu-west-1 --pct 20 --reason "provider flakiness"`
infra-bot: Command accepted: rwctl drain queued (eu-west-1, 20%). ETA 2m for first shift.
emily: toggling reranker now.
emily: `featureset toggle reranker-v2 --region eu-west-1 --off` -> OK. Deploy-bot: rolled back reranker-v2 (canary) in eu-west-1.
olivia: OK reduce per-tenant quotas for heavy tenants in EU immediately: set burst QPS = 20 for tenants > 10k daily tokens. raj can run the script?
raj: running policy patch: `policyctl set-rate --region eu-west-1 --selector "daily_tokens>10000" --qps 20 --burst 40` -> applied.
incident-bot: Rate policy change recorded in incident log.
mike: also start a provider reroute for non-critical traffic to provider Y: `routectl set --region eu-west-1 --path non-critical --provider provider-y --weight 0.6`
jess: routing change applied. Non-critical traffic shifted ~60% to provider Y.
olivia: note: critical enterprise traffic still pinned to provider X for SLA, we cannot move that without CS consent.
support-bot: CS notified enterprise contacts: we offered to failover if they opt in. Waiting on replies.
emily: metrics after actions: 5xx down to 6% within 5 mins, p90 down to 800ms. Memory pressure easing on reranker workers.
raj: ongoing tail: some tokenization edgecases still hitting OOM on older hosts; scheduling upgrade for those hosts in the next hour.
nate: I'm taking the on-call handoff at 10:00 UTC. high-level: 1) reranker disabled in EU, 2) 20% drain in place, 3) rate caps applied to heavy tenants, 4) 60% non-critical traffic to provider Y, 5) CS outreach active.
mike: Nate, your handoff checklist: monitor error_rate(eu-west-1) and provider-Y capacity, rollback route if provider-Y saturates. Also watch enterprise replies for failover opt-in.
nate: ack. I'll keep an eye on capacity and will escalate if provider-Y > 80% util.
jess: temporary node autoscale bumped +15% in eu-west-1 to help absorb shifted traffic.
infra-bot: Autoscaling event: added 6 x g4dn-equivalent instances to eu-west-1 pool at 09:42 UTC.
olivia: customers impacted list (tracked): acme-inc, datawise, small set of consumer apps (metrics sent via CS). We should prepare follow-up postmortem note and action items.
support-bot: logging customer updates to incident ticket IN-18078.
mike: after immediate mitigation, plan: 1) full investigate provider X packet loss root cause, 2) ensure KV cache tuning to avoid thrash under spikes, 3) consider a permanent fallback weight to provider Y for non-critical routes.
emily: also schedule a test of reranker-v2 memory profile against a reproducible load in staging with provider Y.
raj: collecting relevant logs: `s3://redwood-logs/incidents/1807809123/*` - will snapshot for the postmortem.
nate: I'll keep the incident active until error_rate < 1% for 30m and enterprise customers confirm restoration or opt-in to failover. Handing to night oncall for watch.
olivia: thanks team. quick note for postmortem: include timeline, mitigation commands (policyctl, featureset, rwctl, routectl), and customer comms.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations successful so far, monitoring. Next update in 15m or on major change.
support-bot: sent follow-up update to affected customers at 09:55 UTC with mitigations summary and expected next steps.
jess: leaving small reminder: do not re-enable reranker-v2 until we confirm node upgrades and memory patches landed.
raj: will prepare remediation PRs for memory leak and KV cache sizing.
nate: closing notes: oncall handover complete, monitoring aggressive for 2hrs, will post final summary when we meet the recovery threshold.
olivia: good work, everyone. :thumbsup:
